title: Glorification
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Glorification is the final completion of salvation, when God raises and perfects His people in holiness, joy, resurrection life, and eternal fellowship with Him. What God begins in salvation, He will finish in glory.
summary: Glorification is the final completion of salvation, when God raises and perfects His people in holiness, joy, resurrection life, and eternal fellowship with Him. What God begins in salvation, He will finish in glory.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the risen and glorified Lord who will transform His people to be like Him. Believers will share in His resurrection life and behold His glory forever.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Glorification is the believer’s final hope in the order of salvation. God predestines, calls, justifies, and glorifies His people. His saving work will not remain unfinished.

In glorification, believers will be fully freed from sin, weakness, corruption, suffering, and death. They will be made like Christ and raised in glory.

This hope includes the body. Salvation is not escape from embodiment, but resurrection and transformation. Christ will transform the body of humiliation to be conformed to His glorious body.

Glorification magnifies God’s faithfulness. The same grace that begins salvation will complete it, and the same Christ who rose will bring His people into resurrection glory.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers often feel unfinished, weak, and discouraged by remaining sin or bodily suffering. Glorification reminds them that God’s work is not stuck at the present chapter.

For those living with disability, chronic pain, aging, or grief, this doctrine gives concrete hope. God will not merely comfort the body; He will raise and transform His people in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live today in light of final glory. Do not deny present weakness, but do not let it define your final future. Pursue holiness, endure suffering, and encourage the weary with the promise that Christ will complete what He began.
